title: I open sourced a local AI NPC system that can work with any game project
author: Ready_Director_2830
selftext:
I just released a research project I did last year as open source.

It is a fully local speech-to-speech backend for LLM NPCs. So speech-to-text, local LLM, text-to-speech, no cloud needed. The main focus was NPCs talking to each other, not just answering the player, and my study looked at how players experience witnessing those NPC-to-NPC conversations and what it does for immersion.

The NPCs can talk to each other, remember what they said, and later use that context when the player talks to them. There is also a background Game Manager AI that can inject hidden behavioral notes into NPCs to steer the story a bit.

Latency was one of the main technical challenges. With Llama 3.2 3B for VR and 7B on a 4070 Ti I was getting around 400 to 600ms Time to First Audio (TTFA), which is roughly where it starts feeling like a real conversation instead of waiting for the NPC to think. It also runs alongside the Unity scene, which you can see in the demo.

For multiple NPCs, I used a shared generation lock so the GPU does not get overloaded. Each NPC has its own LLM context/personality and TTS setup, but only one generates at a time. They take turns, and the switch between characters is basically instant, so it feels natural. The limitation is that two NPCs cannot literally speak over each other at the exact same moment.

It is WebSocket based, so it should work with Unity, Unreal, or anything else that can talk over WebSockets. I also included the Unity scripts.

I would really like people to try it, build on it, or give feedback. To adapt it to your own game, the main work is tuning the 3-layer NPC prompt setup and the Game Manager prompt. That takes a bit of work, but it is very doable with AI help, and I think a lot of it could be automated later.

Demo video, detective game in Unity:  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z-WZ-Prl8bI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z-WZ-Prl8bI)

Repo:  
[https://github.com/lschiweck/LLM-NPC-Agents](https://github.com/lschiweck/LLM-NPC-Agents)

comments.author: Imaginary-Can6136
comments.body:
Really cool, I have been paranoid about introducing too much complexity into the game I am working on just to keep it able to run on computers with latency issues.

Right now the graphics I am working with are pretty much what you showed in your demo video

could I use your system with an RPG similar in scale to Knights of the old republic or Mass Effect without it causing the player’s computer to crash, or lag too much?

replies.author: Ready_Director_2830
replies.body:
Thank you! To be totally honest, I’ve only tested it with up to around 3 NPCs running at once so far, so I wouldn’t want to claim that it could currently support something on the scale of *Knights of the Old Republic* or *Mass Effect* without issues.

There is definitely some overhead, and performance will likely depend a lot on the player’s hardware, especially VRAM. My study was also done in VR, which added extra performance pressure, and I had to go down to Metas 3B model to keep latency manageable on a single 4070ti with 12GB Vram.

That said, I do think a lot of the current overhead could be reduced with optimization. For a larger RPG, I’d probably recommend limiting how many NPCs are actively “thinking” at once, using smaller or quantized models, caching responses where possible, and only running the system for nearby or important NPCs rather than the whole world at the same time.

So definetly possible and with current level of vibe coding I think nothing is holding you back.
